mnemonic_policy.principle: Mnemonic is a learning story, not an etymological claim.
mnemonic_policy.phono_semantic: Use the semantic component as a meaning anchor and the phonetic component as a sound/shape anchor; do not force the phonetic component meaning into fake etymology.
mnemonic_policy.pictographic_indicative: Use the whole shape as the memory image.

mnemonic_v6.policy: Human-style learner mnemonics. Mnemonic is a memory aid, not a historical etymology claim.

mnemonic_v6_web_verification.note: Kanjipedia analyzes 皆 as 會意 (比 + 白). Cross-source database also records phono-semantic analyses; mnemonic is kept separate from etymology.
Kanjipedia gives 会意形声: 貝 + 网, “collect cowries with a net” -> buy. Supports a vivid learning story while preserving source conflict metadata.
Kanjipedia analyzes old 靜 as 形声 with 爭 as phonetic. This differs from one local role assignment; mnemonic “青/争” remains explicitly a memory story, not etymology.
Kanjipedia traces 風 to 鳳 / wind deity tradition; 虫 is a later graphic development. Do not present “虫 moved by wind” as historical origin.
Kanjipedia gives 羊 + 大 as an ideographic analysis, whereas other sources treat early forms pictographically. Keep conflict explicit.
Kanjipedia gives 形声 禾 + abbreviated phonetic; current 禾+火 story is safe only as mnemonic, not etymology.
Kanjipedia describes 食 pictographically as food in a vessel with a lid, matching the learner-facing whole-shape mnemonic.
Kanjipedia gives 形声: semantic 㕯 and phonetic 章. The storefront/signboard sentence is explicitly a mnemonic, not a literal etymology paraphrase.
Kanjipedia analyzes the older form as 形声 土 + phonetic 𠂹, while other sources in the local aggregate support pictographic analysis. Whole-shape hanging imagery is kept only as a mnemonic.
Kanjipedia traces the old form to a person in a neck restraint; the modern “center” meaning is a borrowed use. The centered-person scene is a learning mnemonic only.
Kanjipedia describes 帝 pictographically as a sacred table/stand for a descended deity, later the supreme deity/ruler. Supports a whole-shape sacred-stand mnemonic.
Kanjipedia describes a river with sandbanks/islets. Supports the river-and-islets whole-shape mnemonic.
Kanjipedia traces 巨 to a carpenter measuring tool; “large” is a borrowed use. Mnemonic keeps the large measuring-tool image without presenting it as semantic origin.
Kanjipedia explicitly describes the sun rising above the horizon. Direct support for the mnemonic.
Kanjipedia explains 幻 via an inverted weaving shuttle / changing patterns and illusion. Supports whole-shape mnemonic; local formation-source conflict remains preserved.
Kanjipedia describes the old form as a decorated belt with cloth hanging down. Direct support for the belt whole-shape mnemonic.
Kanjipedia describes a bird nest on a tree. Direct support for the learner mnemonic.
Kanjipedia traces 己 to the end of a thread; “self” is a borrowed use. The curling-back-to-self sentence is therefore kept explicitly as mnemonic only.
Kanjipedia traces 我 to a serrated saw/tool and says “self” is a borrowed use. The hand/weapon image is a visual mnemonic only, never etymology.
Kanjipedia marks the center of 木 with a stroke; “red” is a borrowed use. The red center-mark story is intentionally mnemonic only.
Kanjipedia describes aligned grain ears, expressing “uniform/equal.” Supports an aligned-shapes mnemonic.
Kanjipedia gives 会意 日 + 比 for “same/kind.” This conflicts with the local selected pictographic claim; mnemonic uses current 日+比 visually and conflict remains explicit.
Kanjipedia gives 形声 with 彡 as semantic and 采 as phonetic. The learner story uses the visible color strokes without changing etymology fields.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a person standing on the ground. Directly supports the whole-shape standing mnemonic.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of small grains arranged on a millet ear; later grain/rice. Supports the grain-image mnemonic.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a large/watchful eye, later servant/retainer. Mnemonic uses the eye image without claiming the modern meaning is pictorially literal.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a deep hollow carved into ground/wood/stone, meaning mortar. Direct support.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a tongue protruding from the mouth. Direct support.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of threads being connected by hand; supports connection/system mnemonic.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of hands twisting threads into rope; search/seek is a borrowed/extended use. Mnemonic keeps rope imagery.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of human/animal hair growing. Direct support.
Kanjipedia: older 𦙪 adds flesh to a shoulder shape. Direct support for body/shoulder mnemonic.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a knife for cutting food; clan/surname is a borrowed use. Mnemonic explicitly uses a knife as a hook for marking a clan, not as etymology.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a long river whose tributary splits from the main stream; supports long-flowing water imagery.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a hanging fur/hide; “seek/want” is a borrowed use. Mnemonic was revised to preserve the hanging-hide image while connecting it to seeking.
Kanjipedia: old 龍 is pictographic, showing a decorated, large-mouthed, long winding reptile/dragon. Supports whole-shape dragon mnemonic.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a sharp spearhead on a long shaft. Direct support.

Kanjipedia classifies 至 as 指事: an arrow reaching/sticking into the ground -> arrive/reach. Local selected formation says pictographic, so this is logged as a source conflict; mnemonic revised to arrow-reaching-ground.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of interlocking roof tiles. Direct support.
Kanjipedia: original form pictographically represents the cross-section/body of a koto with bridges; later phonetic 今 was added. Supports instrument-shape mnemonic.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of armor. Direct support.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a demon/oni holding a whip, hence frighten/fear. Local whole-shape fear mnemonic remains a learning aid.

Kanjipedia classifies 畜 as 会意, 田 + 茲 (increase; 玄 abbreviated), referring to farm animals. Local selected formation says pictographic, so conflict is logged and mnemonic was revised toward animals multiplying in fields.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a bird-catching net; ratio/lead/follow are borrowed uses. Mnemonic revised to keep net imagery and connect it to gathering/leading.
Kanjipedia: old form is phono-semantic 瓦 + phonetic 幷, meaning small earthenware vessel. Supports vessel mnemonic.
Kanjipedia: old form is semantic-phonetic/compound with 至 and 夊, sending/delivering to a destination. Supports reach-and-deliver mnemonic.
Kanjipedia classifies 肘 as 会意, flesh + 寸(hand), while local selected formation is phono-semantic. Conflict is logged; mnemonic focuses on the body joint.
Kanjipedia classifies 華 as 会意形声: 艸 + 𠌶, originally flower/beautiful blossom. Local selected formation is pictographic, so conflict remains logged; mnemonic uses blooming-flower imagery only.
Kanjipedia gives 虞 as fear/worry/apprehension and phono-semantic 虍 + phonetic 吳. Corrected meaning_vi from prior “yên vui, hòa bình” to “lo ngại, e sợ; nguy cơ”.
Kanjipedia: phono-semantic 鬲 + phonetic 蟲 (虫 abbreviated), originally steam/heat, later melt/flow. Fixed component role normalization for 虫 and etymology summary.
Kanjipedia: pictograph of a grass raincoat; weakening is a borrowed meaning. Mnemonic uses the drooping/worn raincoat image as a learning hook.
Kanjipedia: phono-semantic 卜 + phonetic 鼎, divination/asking divine will -> upright/correct. Local selected formation differs; conflict retained.
Kanjipedia: phono-semantic 攴 + phonetic 赤, meaning pardon/forgive. Mnemonic is a visual story and is not presented as etymology.

Kanjipedia: old form is phono-semantic 艸 + 者; historically 著 was also a popular form of 箸 before borrowed uses “write/prominent”. Mnemonic uses current visual form, while historical note stays separate.
Kanjipedia: ideographic 頁 + 彡 originally “beard”; “need/must” is a borrowed use. Mnemonic deliberately uses head-and-beard imagery as a memory hook.
Kanjipedia: 会意形声 鹿 + 丽 (two), originally two deer moving together -> aligned/beautiful. Mnemonic uses paired/cowled deer symmetry.
Kanjipedia: old 默 is phono-semantic 犬 + phonetic 黑, a dog making no sound -> silent. Directly supports the silent-black-dog mnemonic.
Kanjipedia: 会意形声 帛 (silk) + 金 (shining/sound), multicolored gleaming silk. Mnemonic uses silk + metallic shine without claiming a simple one-role decomposition.
Kanjipedia gives an ideographic analysis and also records the theory of ten hand-span/尺 units; final mnemonic avoids presenting one theory as the only etymology.
Kanjipedia classifies 丘 as pictographic, shaped after elevated ground. Local formation source differs, so mnemonic uses whole-shape hill imagery and the conflict is logged.
Kanjipedia traces old 亂 to tangled thread imagery plus 乙; final mnemonic uses tangled-thread imagery rather than the earlier tongue story.
Kanjipedia explains old 乘 as a person standing on a tree, directly supporting the final “get on / be on top” mnemonic.
Kanjipedia notes modern educational 医 derives from a simplified popular form while old 醫 is phono-semantic. Final mnemonic is explicitly a modern visual “medical kit” aid, not etymology.
Kanjipedia gives cloth + sparse weave -> rare, later borrowed for hope/wish. Supports the sparse-cloth learner mnemonic.
Kanjipedia records an ideographic explanation involving avoiding early death / adversity and an alternate handcuff theory; mnemonic uses only the general survival-as-fortune hook.
Kanjipedia gives 口 + a head-turned person, originally a loud voice; Japanese 呉れる “give” is a separate learner-use association, so the final story is labeled mnemonic only.
Kanjipedia gives old form as ideographic 誩 + 羊: auspicious words offered with a sacrificial sheep -> good. Final mnemonic follows that image.
Kanjipedia gives old 器 as many containers 㗊 plus a guard dog 犬 -> important vessels. Directly supports the warehouse/container mnemonic.
Kanjipedia gives old ideographic 𠂹 + 左, uneven/misaligned -> difference. Final mnemonic uses visible misalignment as the learning hook.
Kanjipedia describes teaching/imitating gestures and hands in the old form. Final mnemonic uses a child learning by copying under a school roof.
Kanjipedia gives 帀 + 𠂤, originally a troop surrounding elevated ground, extended to leader/teacher. Final mnemonic uses a group needing a guide.
Kanjipedia treats 肯 as pictographic “meat tightly attached to bone”; agreement/affirmation is a borrowed sense. Final mnemonic uses “firmly attached -> firm yes” as a memory bridge.
Kanjipedia gives 舟 + phonetic 灷, originally caulking a boat; imperial “I” is borrowed. Existing king-on-boat story remains mnemonic only, not etymology.
Kanjipedia classifies 章 as pictographic, originally a tattooing needle/mark; later extended to sections of text/music. Final mnemonic uses “mark -> section/chapter” rather than 音+十 folklore.
Kanjipedia classifies 血 as pictographic blood in a ritual dish. Final mnemonic follows that image; local formation-source disagreement is retained.
Kanjipedia gives 衣 + 毛, fur on the outside of a garment -> outer surface/show. Directly supports final mnemonic.
Kanjipedia gives semantic 臥 + phonetic 品, originally to inspect closely, extended to face/approach. Final mnemonic uses “come close and look down/inspect”.
Kanjipedia gives semantic 林 + phonetic element, with meanings dense growth / blocked mood. Final mnemonic uses dense forest and compressed air as a visual hook.
